evidence.verification: 10 tests pass (2.0 s). Tests compare closed forms with independent integrals and simulation, which is good. Seeded 4 mutants with platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: harmonic(n-k)->harmonic(n-k+1) in exp_order_mean CAUGHT; Poisson-binomial truncation k->k+1 in inclusion_probs CAUGHT; Pareto finiteness guard 'd <= 0' -> 'd < 0' SURVIVED (no test at integer 1/alpha, where the mutant divides by zero); Hajek normaliser '/ w' -> '/ n' SURVIVED (estimators' Hajek output, recommended in the paper as 'a safe default', is never tested). 2 of 4 survived, and no test covers step sizes with rho<=0 (see craft).
evidence.craft: Read src/straggler_backup/model.py (166 lines), tests/test_model.py, experiments/run.py, figure.py. Readable, stdlib-only, docstrings state the maths. Defects: sgd_rounds (model.py:93-105) takes math.log(rho) without guarding rho<=0: `sgd_rounds(64,1.0,1.0,2.0,1.0,0.05)` and eta=1.2 raise 'ValueError: math domain error', and best_k inherits it; E4 avoids it only because its eta grid stops at 0.98. inclusion_probs is a midpoint rule in u with O(n^2 k steps) pure-Python loops yet the paper calls pi_i 'computed exactly' (whitepaper.md:31). `from .model import *` / `from straggler_backup import *` throughout; E4 calls best_k twice per eta for the same value (run.py). Senior reviewer would ask for the rho guard and tests on edge inputs.
evidence.claims: Checked against files: E1 3.0x/1.70x per-round ratios (results.txt 3.015/1.700) backed; E3 table, 34x/1.12x, 33.6x Pareto backed; E4 1.09x-6.91x backed; E5 HT 7-40% worse with no coupling (0.689/0.493=1.40 ... 0.088/0.082=1.07) backed, 21-24% better at k=8-12 (0.244/0.309, 0.109/0.144) backed, tie at k=4 (0.623/0.614) backed. Not backed or wrong: 'fewest workers to drop is ceil(1/alpha)-1' (wrong at integer 1/alpha, whitepaper.md:11 and :36); 'Hajek is a safe default' (whitepaper.md:36) while results.txt shows Hajek worse than plain at k=2 c=1 (1.187 vs 1.107) and in every c=0 row; pi_i 'computed exactly' (numerical midpoint integral); README '~1 min' (observed 5.6 s). The abstract presents the K-sync exponential round-time law and error-runtime trade-off as results 'we give' without citing Dutta et al. 2018, which derived them; related work cites only Dutta et al. 2016 (coded computation).
evidence.fitness: Nearest prior work, checked by knowledge of the literature (not cited in the paper): Dutta, Joshi, Ghosh, Dube, Nagpurkar, 'Slow and Stale Gradients Can Win the Race' (AISTATS 2018) analyses K-sync SGD with exponential and shifted-exponential runtimes, E[X_(K:n)] = (H_n - H_{n-K})/mu, and the error-versus-wall-clock trade-off that gives an interior optimal K - this is the paper's sections 2-3. Pareto order-statistic moments and their finiteness condition are textbook (Arnold, Balakrishnan & Nagaraja 1992), and Wang, Joshi & Wornell (2014-2019) already showed redundancy/cancellation helps more under heavy tails. The speed-data selection bias and its importance-weighting fix are the subject of Cho, Wang & Joshi (AISTATS 2022, biased client selection in FL) and the FL partial-participation literature (unbiased HT-style aggregation, e.g. Chen, Horvath & Richtarik 2020). A researcher could reuse the code as a correct, tested reference, but the results are sound restatements of known results on a 1-D quadratic with single-seed simulations and no real straggler trace; nothing here is new enough for the stated PhD/publishable bar.
evidence.domain: Against the straggler/queueing practice: the order-statistic and Renyi-representation analysis is standard and correctly done; the HT/Hajek estimators are standard survey sampling. Departures a senior reviewer would hit: (1) the SGD model is a 1-D quadratic with a=1 (condition number 1); E4's headline 5.9-6.9x joint (k, eta) gain comes from eta*=0.92 ~ 1/a, where one step nearly solves the problem (`sgd_rounds(39,1.0,0.92,2.0,1.0,0.05)` -> 1 round) - an artefact of the degenerate problem, not a property of backup workers; with a=0.1 my run of best_k over the same grid gives no gain at all (fixed and joint both k*=50, T=398.1). (2) Independent iid-per-round finishing times ignore the persistent per-worker slowness that real clusters show (Dean & Barroso 2013; Google/Alibaba traces), and no real trace is used despite the research brief's real-data expectation. (3) No comparison with hedging/replication or asynchronous/K-async alternatives that the field treats as baselines.

defects.what: Nearest prior work not cited and novelty overstated: Dutta et al. AISTATS 2018 ('Slow and Stale Gradients Can Win the Race') already derives the K-sync exponential round-time law and the error-runtime interior optimum (sections 2-3); the speed-data selection bias and its reweighting fix are covered by Cho, Wang & Joshi AISTATS 2022 and FL partial-participation work; Wang/Joshi/Wornell redundancy analyses and Dean & Barroso 2013 are also absent. The abstract presents these as results 'we give'.

Paper's 'fewest workers to drop for a finite mean is ceil(1/alpha)-1' is wrong whenever 1/alpha is an integer (alpha=0.5 needs 2, paper says 1; alpha=1 needs 1, paper says 0, contradicting the README's own 'alpha<=1 => wait-for-all infinite'); correct is floor(1/alpha). Code is right.

E4's 5.9-6.9x 'joint (k, eta)' gain is an artefact of a 1-D quadratic with a=1: eta*=0.92 ~ 1/a solves it in one round; at a=0.1 the same search gives no gain. Presented as 'the honest comparison' and a general implication (iii).
sgd_rounds takes math.log(rho) with no guard for rho<=0 (eta>=1/a): sgd_rounds(64,1,1.0,2,1,0.05) and best_k raise ValueError: math domain error; E4 avoids it only because its grid stops at 0.98.
Hajek estimator and the integer-1/alpha finiteness boundary are untested: mutants '/ w'->'/ n' and 'd <= 0'->'d < 0' both survive.

'Hajek is a safe default' is contradicted by the committed E5 table (worse than plain at k=2 with coupling, 1.187 vs 1.107, and at every k<16 without); pi_i described as 'computed exactly' though inclusion_probs is a midpoint-rule integral.
README says experiments take ~1 min; they run in 5.6 s.

verdict: A small, clean, correct reference implementation of known results. Every number I recomputed from sources the author did not write (order-statistic density quadrature, the textbook Gamma-form Pareto moments, my own SGD recursion and numpy Monte Carlo for the inclusion probabilities and bias) matches results.txt, and the experiments reproduce byte-identically in 5.6 s. It does not meet the bar: verification is 2 (2 of 4 seeded mutants survive: the Hajek estimator and the Pareto finiteness boundary are untested), claims are 2 (the paper's ceil(1/alpha)-1 rule is wrong at integer 1/alpha, 'Hajek safe default' is contradicted by its own table), and as research it falls short of the PhD bar: the K-sync round-time law and error-runtime optimum are Dutta et al. 2018, the selection bias is Cho/Wang/Joshi 2022, neither is cited, and the headline joint-step gain is an artefact of a condition-number-1 one-dimensional quadratic. Median score 2.
